# Adjudication Task — Chapter 340

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃340화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|중년의 여승, 묘령사태(卯嶺師太)는 파리한 안색으로 힘겹게 입을 열었다.
  6|
  7|“시, 신니께서…… 입적하셨습니다.”
  8|
  9|그 한마디를 듣는 순간, 저절로 주먹에 힘이 들어가고 가슴 한구석이 쿵 하고 내려앉았다.
 10|
 11|불길한 분위기를 알아채고 달려온 청성파의 두 장로가 눈을 부릅뜨며 외쳤다.
 12|
 13|“묘령사태, 그게 무슨 말인가? 신니께서 입적하시다니!”
 14|
 15|“그럴 리 없네! 그럴 리가 없어!”
 16|
 17|신니가 누구를 뜻하는지, 나는 이미 알고 있다.
 18|
 19|그녀 역시 적천강의 기억에 선명히 각인되어 있는 전대의 고수 중 한 사람이었으니까.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|‘성격이 아주 화통했다. 적들 앞에서는 물불 가리지 않았고 무공도 뛰어났어. 굉도, 그 게으름뱅이 땡중보다도 나을 때가 있었지.’
 24|
 25|
 26|
 27|정마대전 당시 마교는 그녀를 혈나찰(血羅剎)이라 부르며 두려워했고, 중원 무림은 경천신니(驚天神尼)라는 별호를 붙여 주었다.
 28|
 29|시간이 흐르고 과거의 영웅들이 하나둘씩 자취를 감춘 그 후에도 그녀는 아미산에 남아 자신의 자리를 지켰다.
 30|
 31|아미파 유일의 초절정 고수이자 존경받는 장문인.
 32|
 33|그런 경천신니가 죽었다.
 34|
 35|‘독왕에 이어 경천신니까지.’
 36|
 37|참 빌어먹을 일이다.
 38|
 39|나는 줄곧 입 안에서 맴돌던 한마디를 내뱉었다.
 40|
 41|“흉수가 누굽니까?”
 42|
 43|“……!”
 44|
 45|“……!”
 46|
 47|묘령사태, 궁기방과 혁무진. 그리고 청성파의 두 장로.
 48|
 49|다섯 사람의 시선이 동시에 나를 향해 쏠린다. 다섯 쌍의 눈동자에 담겨 있는 감정은 놀라움이었지만, 어디에서 기인했는가는 달랐다.
 50|
 51|“흉수라니.”
 52|
 53|“서, 설마 경천신니께서 누군가에게……?”
 54|
 55|청성파의 두 장로는 말을 잇지 못하고 입을 다물었다. 그들도 뒤늦게 깨달은 것이다. 경천신니의 입적 소식에 놀란 탓에 미처 살피지 못했던 묘령사태의 현재 모습을.
 56|
 57|검붉은 핏물이 말라붙은 의복과 푸른 안색.
 58|
 59|커다래진 눈으로 나를 바라보던 그녀가 고개를 푹 떨궜다.
 60|
 61|“역시 진 소협은 알고 있었군요.”
 62|
 63|역시?
 64|
 65|내 눈빛에 궁기방이 무겁게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 66|
 67|“어쩔 수 없었다. 경천신니를 시해한 흉수가…….”
 68|
 69|“사천당문의 그놈과 동일인이거나 연관되어 있겠지. 내 생각도 그래.”
 70|
 71|자신들이 모르는 뭔가가 있다는 것을 알아차린 장로들이 다급한 음성으로 물었다.
 72|
 73|“흉수를 알고 있었다니. 사천당문에도 변고가 벌어졌단 말인가?”
 74|
 75|“하나도 빠짐없이 말하게. 어서!”
 76|
 77|이제는 숨길 수 없다.
 78|
 79|어쩌면 독왕이 살해당했을 때부터 예견되어 있었던 일인지도 모른다.
 80|
 81|나는 크게 심호흡한 뒤 입술을 뗐다.
 82|
 83|“며칠 전, 독왕 당사문 대협께서 돌아가셨습니다. 정확히 말하자면, 누군가에게 살해당했다고 해야겠지만요.”
 84|
 85|“……!”
 86|
 87|“가주이신 만독수라 당사독 대협은 복수를 천명하셨고, 지금쯤 가솔들과 함께 놈을 추격 중일 겁니다.”
 88|
 89|하지만 희생자는 독왕 한 사람으로 끝나지 않았다.
 90|
 91|나는 충격에 빠진 장로들을 뒤로하고, 묘령사태를 똑바로 직시했다.
 92|
 93|“어떻게 된 일입니까?”
 94|
 95|“중년인이었어요. 한쪽 팔이 없는.”
 96|
 97|“외팔이란 말입니까?”
 98|
 99|“네. 그는, 그는…….”
100|
101|묘령사태의 입술 사이로 떨리는 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
102|
103|“악귀(惡鬼), 그 자체였어요.”
104|
105|
106|
107|* * *
108|
109|
110|
111|쉬쉬쉬쉭!
112|
113|거센 바람, 한 걸음을 뻗을 때마다 주위의 풍경이 빠르게 스쳐 지나간다.
114|
115|품에 끌어안은 여승의 무게는 놀랄 만큼 가벼웠고, 맞닿은 몸을 통해 느껴지는 기운은 위태로웠다.
116|
117|‘이런 몸 상태로 여기까지…….’
118|
119|묘령사태는 자신의 이야기를 미처 다 끝내지도 못한 채, 한 바가지의 피를 토하며 혼절했다.
120|
121|한 걸음 뒤에서 바짝 쫓아오고 있는 궁기방이 어두운 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
122|
123|“사태의 부상이 어느 정도인가?”
124|
125|“심각해. 우선 급한 대로 공력을 불어넣어서 생기를 돋우긴 했지만…… 이걸로는 무리야.”
126|
127|궁기방이 작게 신음을 흘렸다.
128|
129|“분명 처음 출발할 때만 해도 이 정도는 아니었는데. 사태께서도 버틸 수 있다고 호언장담하셨다.”
130|
131|“그래도 말렸어야지, 이 자식아.”
132|
133|“……도저히 말릴 수 없었어. 미안하다.”
134|
135|나는 입술을 달싹이다가 이내 꾹 다물어 버렸다.
136|
137|나도 안다. 궁기방과 혁무진이 아니라, 내가 직접 갔어도 묘령사태를 막을 수 없었을 거라는 것을.
138|
139|피를 토하는 와중에도 쥐어짜 낸 그녀의 음성이 아직도 귓가에 생생했다.
140|
141|
142|
143|‘장문인과 세 분의 장로님까지. 모두 악귀의 손에 돌아가셨습니다. 저는, 우리는 웃으며 멀어지는 놈을 쫓을 수 없었어요.’
144|
145|
146|
147|불교의 성지로 불리는 아미산에 악귀가 내려온 것은 불과 사흘 전이라고 했다.
148|
149|여느 참배객처럼 산을 오른 악귀는 경천신니가 기거하는 거처를 찾았고, 때마침 그 자리에는 세 명의 장로가 있었다.
150|
151|그리고 벌어진 경천동지(驚天動地)할 전투. 봉우리가 무너지고 아미산이 몸을 떨었다고 했다.
152|
153|가장 가까이에서 변고를 알아차리고 달려간 묘령사태가 목격한 것은, 이미 숨을 거둔 네 사람의 여승과 한 마리의 악귀였다.
154|
155|
156|
157|‘그리 볼 것 없다. 아미의 불법(佛法)보다 내 살법(殺法)이 강했을 뿐이니.’
158|
159|‘어, 어찌 이런 짓을! 정녕 하늘이 두렵지 않소!’
160|
161|‘우습구나. 너희가 말하는 부처와 하늘은 모두 거짓이요, 허상이다. 내 또 다른 하늘이 있음을 보여 주마.’
162|
163|
164|
165|그것이 마지막이었다.
166|
167|흉수는 묘령사태에게 일장(一掌)을 격중시킨 뒤 사라졌고, 슬픔과 분노에 휩싸인 아미파에 두 청년이 찾아왔다.
168|
169|궁기방과 혁무진으로부터 청성파가 가까이 있다는 이야기를 들은 그녀는 사람들의 만류를 뿌리치고 아미산을 내려왔다.
170|
171|
172|
173|‘도와주십시오. 제발 도와주십시오! 무슨 일이 있어도 반드시 그 악귀를…… 쿨럭!’
174|
175|
176|
177|의식을 잃던 마지막 순간까지 부르짖던 묘령사태의 모습을 떠올리니, 저절로 이가 악물렸다.
178|
179|‘도대체 어떤 놈이냐…….’
180|
181|외팔의 중년인. 전대의 초절정 고수인 경천신니와 세 장로를 단신으로 죽일 만큼 가공할 무위(武威)의 소유자.
182|
183|놈은 어떤 목적으로, 왜 이런 일을 벌인 걸까. 그리고 놈이 독왕 당사문을 살해한 그 흉수와 동일인일까.
184|
185|‘만약에 동일인이 아니라면?’
186|
187|생각에 거기에까지 미치자, 순간 등골이 서늘해지고 심장이 거세게 뛰었다.
188|
189|만약 두 사건의 흉수가 각각 다른 인물이라면…… 사천 땅이 사지(死地)로 변하는 건 시간문제다.
190|
191|막힘없이 나아가던 발걸음이 무거워지던 그때, 청성파의 두 장로가 입을 열었다.
192|
193|“이쯤에서 헤어져야 할 것 같네.”
194|
195|“자네에게는 미안하네만, 지금으로서는 사정이 여의치 않아.”
196|
197|사문이 염려되는 그들에게는 당연한 선택이었다.
198|
199|사천당문에 이어 아미파까지 당했다. 바보가 아닌 이상 누구라도 다음이 청성파의 차례라는 걸 짐작할 수 있었다.
200|
201|“사과하실 필요 없습니다. 저라도 그렇게 했을 거예요.”
202|
203|“이해해 줘서 고맙군.”
204|
205|“곧장 청성산으로 가실 생각이십니까?”
206|
207|더 나이가 많은 장로가 고개를 저었다.
208|
209|“노부는 제자들 일부를 인솔하여 아미파를 도우러 걸세. 사제는 나머지 제자들과 함께 본산으로 귀환할 것이고. 자네는?”
210|
211|“묘령사태께서 입은 부상이 생각보다 심각해서요. 의원을 찾은 다음, 사천당문에 연락을 취할 생각입니다.”
212|
213|현재 문파의 상당수가 빠져나간 사천당문과 청성파는 무주공산(無主空山)과 같다. 만일을 대비해 경고해 줘야 한다.
214|
215|사문이 같은 입장에 처한 장로가 그것을 모를 리 없었다.
216|
217|“일단은 묘령사태를 치료하는 것에 집중하게. 사천당문에는 우리 쪽에서 사람을 보내 놓지.”
218|
219|“감사합니다.”
220|
221|“천만에. 무운(武運)을 빌겠네.”
222|
223|“저 역시.”
224|
225|서로를 향해 포권을 취한 우리는 세 갈래로 갈라졌다.
226|
227|두 장로가 제자들을 인솔하여 각각 북쪽과 동쪽으로 사라지자, 남은 사람은 나를 포함한 넷뿐이었다.
228|
229|‘아, 적천강과 묘령사태도 있었지.’
230|
231|환자를 고치러 사천까지 왔는데, 신의는커녕 환자가 한 명 더 늘었다.
232|
233|‘뭐지, 몰래 카메라인가.’
234|
235|시벌, 그럴 리가 있나.
236|
237|내심 깊은 한숨을 내쉬며 재차 걸음을 떼려던 그 순간이었다.
238|
239|저벅. 저벅.
240|
241|흙을 밟으며 올라오는 사뿐한 걸음걸이와 경쾌하게 흥얼거리는 콧노래 소리. 산길을 따라 올라오던 소년 하나가, 마침내 우리를 발견하고 눈을 크게 떴다.
242|
243|“어? 어어?”
244|
245|낯익은 얼굴. 소년의 이름은 문경이었다.
246|
247|나는 불과 며칠 만에 다시 만난 녀석이 반가웠지만, 그보다는 앞서 한 가지 생각이 머리를 스쳤다.
248|
249|“문경아.”
250|
251|“다들 이곳에는 어쩐 일로…… 네?”
252|
253|“너, 의생 맞지?”
254|
255|아직 기억하고 있다. 쾌조선의 갑판에서 진료를 봐주던 녀석의 모습을.
256|
257|정확히 어떤 치료를 했는지는 모르지만, 수적들의 말에 의하면 제법 실력도 뛰어난 수준이다.
258|
259|“네에. 그렇긴 합니다만…….”
260|
261|얼떨떨한 표정으로 대답한 문경의 시선이 내 품에 안긴 묘령사태를 향했다. 그것으로 더 이상의 설명은 필요 없어졌다.
262|
263|녀석이 품에 들고 있던 행낭에서 침구(鍼灸)가 든 목갑을 꺼내며 성큼 다가왔으니까.
264|
265|“우선…… 환자 상태부터 볼까요.”
266|
267|
268|
269|* * *
270|
271|
272|
273|스스슥.
274|
275|맥을 짚고, 침을 놓기까지 걸린 시간은 촌각에 불과했다.
276|
277|하지만 그 모든 과정을 물 흐르듯 매끄럽게 처리했음에도, 문경의 얼굴에는 그늘이 깔려 있었다.
278|
279|“……어때?”
280|
281|결과가 썩 좋지 않으리라는 것은 굳이 물어보지 않아도 알 수 있었다.
282|
283|아니나 다를까, 문경이 작게 고개를 가로젓는다.
284|
285|“좋지 않아요. 정말로.”
286|
287|“최소한의 치료는 된 거지?”
288|
289|“예.”
290|
291|나는 안도의 한숨을 내쉬었다.
292|
293|문경에게는 미안한 말이지만, 어차피 처음부터 큰 기대는 하지 않았다. 녀석은 나이도 어리고, 의술에 발을 들인 기간도 그만큼 짧으니까.
294|
295|내가 원했던 것은 바로 그 최소한의 치료였다.
296|
297|“고생했다. 지금은 그걸로 충분해. 최대한 빨리 성도로 가서 방법을 찾으면…….”
298|
299|“정말 그럴까요?”
300|
301|“뭐?”
302|
303|“한 달 후면 살이 문드러지고, 넉 달 후에는 뼈가 녹아내릴 겁니다.”
304|
305|“잠깐만. 인마, 너 지금 무슨 소리…….”
306|

“I’m sorry, but circumstances leave us no other choice.”

[P88]
It was only natural for them to worry about their own sect.

[P89]
First the Sichuan Tang Clan, and now the Emei Sect. Anyone with a brain could guess that the Qingcheng Sect might be next.

[P90]
“There’s no need to apologize. I would do the same.”

[P91]
“Thank you for understanding.”

[P92]
“Are you going straight to Mount Qingcheng?”

[P93]
The older of the two Elders shook his head.

[P94]
“I will lead some of our Disciples to assist the Emei Sect. My Junior Brother will return to the main sect with the remaining Disciples. What about you?”

[P95]
“Venerable Myoryeong’s injuries are worse than I thought. I intend to find a physician first, then contact the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

[P96]
With so many of their members away, the Sichuan Tang Clan and the Qingcheng Sect had both been left virtually undefended. They needed to be warned, just in case.

[P97]
The Elder, whose own sect was in the same position, understood that perfectly well.

[P98]
“For now, focus on treating Venerable Myoryeong. We will send someone to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

[P99]
“Thank you.”

[P100]
“Think nothing of it. May fortune favor your martial path.”

[P101]
“And yours.”

[P102]
We exchanged martial salutes and split into three groups.

[P103]
The two Elders led their respective groups of Disciples north and east, leaving only four people, including me.

[P104]
*Ah. Jeok Cheongang and Venerable Myoryeong were here too.*

[P105]
We had come all the way to Sichuan to heal one patient, but instead of finding the Divine Physician, we had gained another.

[P106]
*What is this, some kind of hidden-camera prank?*

[P107]
Fuck, as if.

[P108]
I heaved an inward sigh and was about to start walking again when—

[P109]
*Step. Step.*

[P110]
Light footsteps came up the dirt path, accompanied by cheerful humming. A boy climbing the mountain trail finally spotted us and opened his eyes wide.

[P111]
“Huh? Wha—?”

[P112]
It was a familiar face. The boy’s name was Mungyeong.

[P113]
I was glad to see him again after only a few days, but before that feeling could fully surface, another thought flashed through my mind.

[P114]
“Mungyeong.”

[P115]
“What brings everyone here…? Huh?”

[P116]
“You’re a medical apprentice, right?”

[P117]
I still remembered him treating people on the deck of the swift ship.

[P118]
I did not know exactly what treatment he had provided, but according to the river bandits, he was quite skilled.

[P119]
“Yeees. I am, but…”

[P120]
Mungyeong answered with a bewildered expression, then looked at Venerable Myoryeong in my arms. No further explanation was necessary.

[P121]
He pulled a wooden case of acupuncture and moxibustion tools from the travel bag in his arms and strode toward us.

[P122]
“First… let me examine the patient.”

[P123]
* * *

[P124]
*Rustle.*

[P125]
It took Mungyeong only moments to check her pulse and insert the needles.

[P126]
Yet despite handling the entire process with effortless fluidity, a shadow hung over his face.

[P127]
“…How is she?”

[P128]
I did not need to ask to know the answer would not be good.

[P129]
Sure enough, Mungyeong quietly shook his head.

[P130]
“Not good. Not at all.”

[P131]
“You managed to give her some basic treatment, right?”

[P132]
“Yes.”

[P133]
I let out a sigh of relief.

[P134]
It might have been unkind, but I had never expected much from Mungyeong in the first place. He was young and had only been studying medicine for a short time.

[P135]
Basic treatment was all I had wanted from him.

[P136]
“You did well. That’s enough for now. If we get to Chengdu as quickly as possible and find a way…”

[P137]
“Will that really be enough?”

[P138]
“What?”

[P139]
“In one month, her flesh will begin to rot. In four months, her bones will melt away.”

[P140]
“Hold on. What the hell are you talking about…?”

[P141]
But Mungyeong continued in the same quiet voice.

[P142]
“After half a year of horrific pain, she will look like a living corpse. She might survive a year at most. Once her organs begin to rot, she will finally stop breathing.”

[P143]
“…What?”

[P144]
“Even if you take her to Chengdu, you won’t find any suitable treatment. The physicians available among the common people can only handle women’s ailments of the sort suffered by high officials and nobles. And the Sichuan Tang Clan…”

[P145]
Two things shocked me.

[P146]
First, that Venerable Myoryeong’s injuries were so severe.

[P147]
Second, the unfamiliar sight of Mungyeong calmly describing something so horrifying.

[P148]
“I heard rumors all over the marketplace that the Tang Clan’s martial artists had headed west. It will take them several days at least to return. By then, it will be too late. How long ago was she injured?”

[P149]
Hyuk Mujin answered haltingly.

[P150]
“Th-Three days. A little over three days, I think.”

[P151]
“Three days…”

[P152]
Mungyeong let out a quiet groan, then continued in a heavy voice.

[P153]
“The Black Hand Seal is a terrifying evil technique. Once seven days and nights have passed, there will be no turning back.”

[P154]
*Grab!*

[P155]
That was as far as he got.

[P156]
My patience snapped. Unable to hold back any longer, I seized him by the collar.

[P157]
“You… How the hell do you know that?”

[P158]
A teenage medical apprentice had just named an evil technique no one else present had ever heard of.

[P159]
The Mungyeong I knew could never have possessed such knowledge.

[P160]
“Tell me. Now.”

[P161]
Mungyeong swallowed at the chill in my aura before answering.

[P162]
“My Master… My Master taught me everything.”

[P163]
“Your Master?”

[P164]
“Y-Yes. Yes… Cough!”

[P165]
A flash of realization streaked through my mind.

[P166]
The strength drained from the hand gripping his collar.

[P167]
A murmur like a groan slipped from my lips.

[P168]
“The Divine Physician…?”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P95]
“Venerable Myoryeong’s injuries are worse than I thought. I intend to find a physician first, then contact the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

[P96]
With so many of their members away, the Sichuan Tang Clan and the Qingcheng Sect had both been left virtually undefended. They needed to be warned, just in case.

[P97]
The Elder, whose own sect was in the same position, understood that perfectly well.

[P98]
“For now, focus on treating Venerable Myoryeong. We will send someone to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

[P99]
“Thank you.”

[P100]
“Think nothing of it. May fortune favor your martial path.”

[P101]
“And yours.”

[P102]
We exchanged martial salutes and split into three groups.

[P103]
The two Elders led their respective groups of Disciples north and east, leaving only four people, including me.

[P104]
*Ah. Jeok Cheongang and Venerable Myoryeong were here too.*

[P105]
We had come all the way to Sichuan to heal one patient, but instead of finding the Divine Physician, we had gained another.

[P106]
*What is this, some kind of hidden-camera prank?*

[P107]
Fuck, as if.

[P108]
I heaved an inward sigh and was about to start walking again when—

[P109]
*Step. Step.*

[P110]
Light footsteps came up the dirt path, accompanied by cheerful humming. A boy climbing the mountain trail finally spotted us and opened his eyes wide.

[P111]
“Huh? Wha—?”

[P112]
It was a familiar face. The boy’s name was Mungyeong.

[P113]
I was glad to see him again after only a few days, but before that feeling could fully surface, another thought flashed through my mind.

[P114]
“Mungyeong.”

[P115]
“What brings everyone here…? Huh?”

[P116]
“You’re a medical apprentice, right?”

[P117]
I still remembered him treating people on the deck of the swift ship.

[P118]
I did not know exactly what treatment he had provided, but according to the river bandits, he was quite skilled.

[P119]
“Yeees. I am, but…”

[P120]
Mungyeong answered with a bewildered expression, then looked at Venerable Myoryeong in my arms. No further explanation was necessary.

[P121]
He pulled a wooden case of acupuncture and moxibustion tools from the travel bag in his arms and strode toward us.

[P122]
“First… let me examine the patient.”

[P123]
* * *

[P124]
*Rustle.*

[P125]
It took Mungyeong only moments to check her pulse and insert the needles.

[P126]
Yet despite handling the entire process with effortless fluidity, a shadow hung over his face.

[P127]
“…How is she?”

[P128]
I did not need to ask to know the answer would not be good.

[P129]
Sure enough, Mungyeong quietly shook his head.

[P130]
“Not good. Not at all.”

[P131]
“You managed to give her some basic treatment, right?”

[P132]
“Yes.”

[P133]
I let out a sigh of relief.

[P134]
It might have been unkind, but I had never expected much from Mungyeong in the first place. He was young and had only been studying medicine for a short time.

[P135]
Basic treatment was all I had wanted from him.

[P136]
“You did well. That’s enough for now. If we get to Chengdu as quickly as possible and find a way…”

[P137]
“Will that really be enough?”

[P138]
“What?”

[P139]
“In one month, her flesh will begin to rot. In four months, her bones will melt away.”

[P140]
“Hold on. What the hell are you talking about…?”

[P141]
But Mungyeong continued in the same quiet voice.

[P142]
“After half a year of horrific pain, she will look like a living corpse. She might survive a year at most. Once her organs begin to rot, she will finally stop breathing.”

[P143]
“…What?”

[P144]
“Even if you take her to Chengdu, you won’t find any suitable treatment. The physicians available among the common people can only handle women’s ailments of the sort suffered by high officials and nobles. And the Sichuan Tang Clan…”

[P145]
Two things shocked me.

[P146]
First, that Venerable Myoryeong’s injuries were so severe.

[P147]
Second, the unfamiliar sight of Mungyeong calmly describing something so horrifying.

[P148]
“I heard rumors all over the marketplace that the Tang Clan’s martial artists had headed west. It will take them several days at least to return. By then, it will be too late. How long ago was she injured?”

[P149]
Hyuk Mujin answered haltingly.

[P150]
“Th-Three days. A little over three days, I think.”

[P151]
“Three days…”

[P152]
Mungyeong let out a quiet groan, then continued in a heavy voice.

[P153]
“The Black Hand Seal is a terrifying evil technique. Once seven days and nights have passed, there will be no turning back.”

[P154]
*Grab!*

[P155]
That was as far as he got.

[P156]
My patience snapped. Unable to hold back any longer, I seized him by the collar.

[P157]
“You… How the hell do you know that?”

[P158]
A teenage medical apprentice had just named an evil technique no one else present had ever heard of.

[P159]
The Mungyeong I knew could never have possessed such knowledge.

[P160]
“Tell me. Now.”

[P161]
Mungyeong swallowed at the chill in my aura before answering.

[P162]
“My Master… My Master taught me everything.”

[P163]
“Your Master?”

[P164]
“Y-Yes. Yes… Cough!”

[P165]
A flash of realization streaked through my mind.

[P166]
The strength drained from the hand gripping his collar.

[P167]
A murmur like a groan slipped from my lips.

[P168]
“The Divine Physician…?”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 340

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃340화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|중년의 여승, 묘령사태(卯嶺師太)는 파리한 안색으로 힘겹게 입을 열었다.
  6|
  7|“시, 신니께서…… 입적하셨습니다.”
  8|
  9|그 한마디를 듣는 순간, 저절로 주먹에 힘이 들어가고 가슴 한구석이 쿵 하고 내려앉았다.
 10|
 11|불길한 분위기를 알아채고 달려온 청성파의 두 장로가 눈을 부릅뜨며 외쳤다.
 12|
 13|“묘령사태, 그게 무슨 말인가? 신니께서 입적하시다니!”
 14|
 15|“그럴 리 없네! 그럴 리가 없어!”
 16|
 17|신니가 누구를 뜻하는지, 나는 이미 알고 있다.
 18|
 19|그녀 역시 적천강의 기억에 선명히 각인되어 있는 전대의 고수 중 한 사람이었으니까.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|‘성격이 아주 화통했다. 적들 앞에서는 물불 가리지 않았고 무공도 뛰어났어. 굉도, 그 게으름뱅이 땡중보다도 나을 때가 있었지.’
 24|
 25|
 26|
 27|정마대전 당시 마교는 그녀를 혈나찰(血羅剎)이라 부르며 두려워했고, 중원 무림은 경천신니(驚天神尼)라는 별호를 붙여 주었다.
 28|
 29|시간이 흐르고 과거의 영웅들이 하나둘씩 자취를 감춘 그 후에도 그녀는 아미산에 남아 자신의 자리를 지켰다.
 30|
 31|아미파 유일의 초절정 고수이자 존경받는 장문인.
 32|
 33|그런 경천신니가 죽었다.
 34|
 35|‘독왕에 이어 경천신니까지.’
 36|
 37|참 빌어먹을 일이다.
 38|
 39|나는 줄곧 입 안에서 맴돌던 한마디를 내뱉었다.
 40|
 41|“흉수가 누굽니까?”
 42|
 43|“……!”
 44|
 45|“……!”
 46|
 47|묘령사태, 궁기방과 혁무진. 그리고 청성파의 두 장로.
 48|
 49|다섯 사람의 시선이 동시에 나를 향해 쏠린다. 다섯 쌍의 눈동자에 담겨 있는 감정은 놀라움이었지만, 어디에서 기인했는가는 달랐다.
 50|
 51|“흉수라니.”
 52|
 53|“서, 설마 경천신니께서 누군가에게……?”
 54|
 55|청성파의 두 장로는 말을 잇지 못하고 입을 다물었다. 그들도 뒤늦게 깨달은 것이다. 경천신니의 입적 소식에 놀란 탓에 미처 살피지 못했던 묘령사태의 현재 모습을.
 56|
 57|검붉은 핏물이 말라붙은 의복과 푸른 안색.
 58|
 59|커다래진 눈으로 나를 바라보던 그녀가 고개를 푹 떨궜다.
 60|
 61|“역시 진 소협은 알고 있었군요.”
 62|
 63|역시?
 64|
 65|내 눈빛에 궁기방이 무겁게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 66|
 67|“어쩔 수 없었다. 경천신니를 시해한 흉수가…….”
 68|
 69|“사천당문의 그놈과 동일인이거나 연관되어 있겠지. 내 생각도 그래.”
 70|
 71|자신들이 모르는 뭔가가 있다는 것을 알아차린 장로들이 다급한 음성으로 물었다.
 72|
 73|“흉수를 알고 있었다니. 사천당문에도 변고가 벌어졌단 말인가?”
 74|
 75|“하나도 빠짐없이 말하게. 어서!”
 76|
 77|이제는 숨길 수 없다.
 78|
 79|어쩌면 독왕이 살해당했을 때부터 예견되어 있었던 일인지도 모른다.
 80|
 81|나는 크게 심호흡한 뒤 입술을 뗐다.
 82|
 83|“며칠 전, 독왕 당사문 대협께서 돌아가셨습니다. 정확히 말하자면, 누군가에게 살해당했다고 해야겠지만요.”
 84|
 85|“……!”
 86|
 87|“가주이신 만독수라 당사독 대협은 복수를 천명하셨고, 지금쯤 가솔들과 함께 놈을 추격 중일 겁니다.”
 88|
 89|하지만 희생자는 독왕 한 사람으로 끝나지 않았다.
 90|
 91|나는 충격에 빠진 장로들을 뒤로하고, 묘령사태를 똑바로 직시했다.
 92|
 93|“어떻게 된 일입니까?”
 94|
 95|“중년인이었어요. 한쪽 팔이 없는.”
 96|
 97|“외팔이란 말입니까?”
 98|
 99|“네. 그는, 그는…….”
100|
101|묘령사태의 입술 사이로 떨리는 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
102|
103|“악귀(惡鬼), 그 자체였어요.”
104|
105|
106|
107|* * *
108|
109|
110|
111|쉬쉬쉬쉭!
112|
113|거센 바람, 한 걸음을 뻗을 때마다 주위의 풍경이 빠르게 스쳐 지나간다.
114|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
